name: Reading assistant
summary: Answers readers' questions from the fictional publisher's own archive, with sources.
problem: Readers searched an archive of twenty years by keywords and rarely found the article they remembered.
workDone: Designed retrieval over the archive with pgvector, a small answering agent and an evaluation suite of two hundred real-looking questions.
result: Four in five test questions are answered with a correct source; the suite runs on every change.

cover.altText: A placeholder cover for the reading assistant.

caseStudy.body:
## Context

The **fictional** Lumen Press wanted readers to find old articles by asking, not by guessing keywords.

## Approach

We wrote the evaluation questions first, then tried three chunking strategies against them. The agent may only answer with a cited article and says so when it cannot.

## Outcome

The assistant shipped to a test group; the evaluation suite now guards every change to prompts, chunking and models.

name: Editorial workbench
summary: One back office for planning, editing and publishing the fictional publisher's stories.
problem: Editors juggled three tools and a shared spreadsheet to publish one story.
workDone: Built a Next.js workbench over one PostgreSQL schema, with drafts, review and scheduled publishing.
result: Publishing a story takes one tool and half the steps.

cover.altText: A placeholder cover for the editorial workbench.

caseStudy.body:
## Context

A **fictional** newsroom with three tools and one spreadsheet.

## Approach

Interviews with six editors, a shared data model first and a workbench released one desk at a time.

## Outcome

The old tools were switched off after four months.

name: Headline tester
summary: A small tool that compares headline variants on a share of the fictional readership.
problem: Headline choices were made by gut feeling.
workDone: Added variant assignment at the edge and a daily report.
result: Editors test two headlines a day on average.

name: Store replatforming
summary: Moved the fictional retailer's online store to a TypeScript API and a React front end.
problem: Every change to the old store risked the checkout.
workDone: Strangled the monolith route by route behind a GraphQL API, with contract tests for each route.
result: Releases went from monthly to daily without a checkout outage.

cover.altText: A placeholder cover for the store replatforming.

name: Warehouse picking
summary: Handheld picking lists for the fictional retailer's two warehouses.
problem: Pickers walked the warehouse in the order orders arrived.
workDone: Built a picking service that groups orders by aisle and a small handheld front end.
result: Pickers walk about a third less per shift.

cover.altText: A placeholder cover for warehouse picking.

name: Booking portal
summary: The fictional freight company's portal for booking and tracking shipments.
problem: Customers booked shipments by e-mail and phoned to track them.
workDone: Extended the Symfony portal with online booking and live tracking from carrier feeds.
result: Most bookings arrive through the portal.

name: Document assistant prototype
summary: A prototype assistant that answers staff questions from a fictional firm's handbooks.
problem: Staff of a small accounting firm asked the same handbook questions every week.
workDone: Built a prototype exposing the handbooks to an assistant through an MCP server, with a short evaluation set.
result: The firm kept the prototype for internal use.

name: Architecture review kit
summary: A repeatable checklist and report template for reviewing small web platforms.
problem: Each review started from a blank page.
workDone: Collected the questions of earlier reviews into a checklist and a report template.
result: A review takes two days instead of five.

name: Community catalogue
summary: An open-source catalogue for fictional community libraries.
problem: Small libraries kept their catalogue in spreadsheets.
workDone: Maintains the React front end and its Playwright suite.
result: Used by a dozen fictional libraries.
